claim: The brains of Alzheimer's disease patients show a decrease in brain mass.
source: The brains of Alzheimer's disease patients show a decrease in brain mass and a preponderance of extracellular Amyloid-β plaques.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract presenting established knowledge about AD pathology.

claim: The brains of Alzheimer's disease patients show a preponderance of extracellular Amyloid-β plaques.
source: The brains of Alzheimer's disease patients show a decrease in brain mass and a preponderance of extracellular Amyloid-β plaques.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract presenting established knowledge about AD pathology.

claim: Amyloid-β plaques are formed by aggregation of polypeptides that are derived from the Amyloid Precursor Protein (APP).
source: These plaques are formed by aggregation of polypeptides that are derived from the Amyloid Precursor Protein (APP).
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract presenting established knowledge about the origin of Aβ plaques.

claim: Amyloid-β plaques are thought to play either a direct or an indirect role in disease progression.
source: Amyloid-β plaques are thought to play either a direct or an indirect role in disease progression, however the exact role of aggregation and plaque formation in the aetiology of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is subject to debate as the biological effects of soluble and aggregated Amyloid-β peptides are difficult to separate in vivo.
evidence: This statement reflects current scientific debate and uncertainty in the field.

claim: The exact role of aggregation and plaque formation in the aetiology of Alzheimer's disease is subject to debate.
source: Amyloid-β plaques are thought to play either a direct or an indirect role in disease progression, however the exact role of aggregation and plaque formation in the aetiology of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is subject to debate as the biological effects of soluble and aggregated Amyloid-β peptides are difficult to separate in vivo.
evidence: This statement reflects current scientific debate and uncertainty in the field.

claim: The biological effects of soluble and aggregated Amyloid-β peptides are difficult to separate in vivo.
source: Amyloid-β plaques are thought to play either a direct or an indirect role in disease progression, however the exact role of aggregation and plaque formation in the aetiology of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is subject to debate as the biological effects of soluble and aggregated Amyloid-β peptides are difficult to separate in vivo.
evidence: This statement reflects a technical challenge in the field that motivates the study.

claim: A fluorescently tagged, optogenetic Amyloid-β peptide was developed that oligomerizes rapidly in the presence of blue light.
source: To investigate the consequences of formation of Amyloid-β oligomers in living tissues, we developed a fluorescently tagged, optogenetic Amyloid-β peptide that oligomerizes rapidly in the presence of blue light.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study describing the development of a novel tool.

claim: Both expression and induced oligomerization of Amyloid-β were detrimental to lifespan and healthspan in Drosophila, C. elegans and D. rerio.
source: We use Drosophila, C. elegans and D. rerio to show that, although both expression and induced oligomerization of Amyloid-β were detrimental to lifespan and healthspan, we were able to separate the metabolic and physical damage caused by light-induced Amyloid-β oligomerization from Amyloid-β expression alone.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data from multiple model organisms.

claim: The metabolic and physical damage caused by light-induced Amyloid-β oligomerization can be separated from Amyloid-β expression alone.
source: We use Drosophila, C. elegans and D. rerio to show that, although both expression and induced oligomerization of Amyloid-β were detrimental to lifespan and healthspan, we were able to separate the metabolic and physical damage caused by light-induced Amyloid-β oligomerization from Amyloid-β expression alone.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data showing differential effects.

claim: The physical damage caused by Amyloid-β oligomers recapitulated the catastrophic tissue loss that is a hallmark of late AD.
source: The physical damage caused by Amyloid-β oligomers also recapitulated the catastrophic tissue loss that is a hallmark of late AD.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental observations.

claim: The lifespan deficit induced by Amyloid-β oligomers was reduced with Li+ treatment.
source: We show that the lifespan deficit induced by Amyloid-β oligomers was reduced with Li+ treatment.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data from drug treatment.

claim: Alzheimer's disease affects more than 46.8 million people worldwide.
source: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a debilitating, age-associated, neurodegenerative disease which affects more than 46.8 million people worldwide and represents the 6th leading cause of death in the United States of America (Ahn et al., 2001; De-Paula et al., 2012; Hawkes, 2016; Kumar et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Alzheimer's disease represents the 6th leading cause of death in the United States of America.
source: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a debilitating, age-associated, neurodegenerative disease which affects more than 46.8 million people worldwide and represents the 6th leading cause of death in the United States of America (Ahn et al., 2001; De-Paula et al., 2012; Hawkes, 2016; Kumar et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: No disease-modifying therapy has been found for Alzheimer's disease despite extensive efforts over the last 50 years.
source: Despite extensive efforts over the last 50 years, no disease-modifying therapy has been found and, most recently, several high-profile Phase III clinical trials have failed (Anderson et al., 2017; Lim and Mathuru, 2018; Park et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Several high-profile Phase III clinical trials for Alzheimer's disease have failed.
source: Despite extensive efforts over the last 50 years, no disease-modifying therapy has been found and, most recently, several high-profile Phase III clinical trials have failed (Anderson et al., 2017; Lim and Mathuru, 2018; Park et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: More than 50% of the drugs in Phase III trials for Alzheimer's disease target amyloid beta.
source: The AD clinical trial landscape has largely been dominated by the amyloid cascade hypothesis, with more than 50% of the drugs targeting amyloid beta (Aβ) in Phase III trials alone (Cummings et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The amyloid cascade hypothesis posits the deposition of Aβ, in particular the extracellular Aβ plaque, as the main driver of AD.
source: The amyloid cascade hypothesis, in its original form, posits the deposition of Aβ, in particular the extracellular Aβ plaque, as the main driver of AD (Hardy and Higgins, 1992).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the original hypothesis.

claim: The causative role of Aβ plaques has recently been challenged.
source: However, the causative role of Aβ plaques has recently been challenged, because of the failure of numerous interventions targeting Aβ plaques in Phase III trials and the observation of Aβ plaques in brains of non-AD symptomatic individuals (Cummings, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Aβ plaques have been observed in brains of non-AD symptomatic individuals.
source: However, the causative role of Aβ plaques has recently been challenged, because of the failure of numerous interventions targeting Aβ plaques in Phase III trials and the observation of Aβ plaques in brains of non-AD symptomatic individuals (Cummings, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: AD pathology can be modeled in the absence of obvious Aβ plaques in model organisms ranging from nematodes to mice.
source: Model organisms ranging from nematodes to mice have further shown that AD pathology can be modeled in the absence of obvious Aβ plaques (Duff et al., 1996; Fong et al., 2016; Teo et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Intracellular accumulation of Aβ may be a mechanism for Aβ neurotoxicity.
source: These observations point to a different mechanism for Aβ neurotoxicity perhaps through Aβ's intracellular accumulation (LaFerla et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature and represents an inference from observations.

claim: Soluble Aβ oligomers appear to be the main toxic species in AD.
source: Of these, soluble Aβ oligomers appear to be the main toxic species in AD (Ferreira and Klein, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Aβ oligomers have been shown to induce neurotoxic effects including memory loss in transgenic animal models.
source: For example, Aβ oligomers have been shown to induce neurotoxic effects including memory loss in transgenic animal models reviewed in Mroczko et al. (2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Studies on Aβ oligomers mostly rely on in vitro injection of synthetic Aβ oligomers or oligomers extracted from AD brains.
source: These studies, however, mostly rely on in vitro injection of synthetic Aβ oligomers or oligomers extracted from AD brains (Mroczko et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: There is currently a lack of tools that can directly control Aβ oligomerization in vivo.
source: There is currently a lack of tools that can directly control Aβ oligomerization in vivo, which would allow direct examination of the effects of Aβ oligomerization.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of the field and motivates the study.

claim: A modified version of the Arabidopsis thaliana cryptochrome 2 (CRY2) protein oligomerizes into photobodies quickly and reversibly in the presence of blue light at 488 nm.
source: One such optogenetic protein, a modified version of the Arabidopsis thaliana cryptochrome 2 (CRY2) protein, oligomerizes into photobodies quickly and reversibly in the presence of blue light at 488 nm (Más et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Expression of the photolyase homology region of CRY2 fused to mCherry led to puncta within 10 s of exposure to blue light in cultured cells.
source: In cultured cells, expression of the photolyase homology region of CRY2 fused to mCherry led to puncta within 10 s of exposure to blue light and these puncta dispersed within minutes (Bugaj et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: CRY2-mCherry puncta dispersed within minutes after blue light exposure in cultured cells.
source: In cultured cells, expression of the photolyase homology region of CRY2 fused to mCherry led to puncta within 10 s of exposure to blue light and these puncta dispersed within minutes (Bugaj et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: CRY2-mCherry has been used to study cortical actin dynamics in cell contractility during tissue morphogenesis.
source: This basic unit of CRY2-mCherry attached to a variety of proteins have, for instance, been used to study cortical actin dynamics in cell contractility during tissue morphogenesis, the dynamics of Wnt and EGF signaling, plasma membrane composition and transcriptional regulation (Bugaj et al., 2018; Bugaj et al., 2015; Guglielmi et al., 2015; Huang et al., 2017; Idevall-Hagren et al., 2012; Johnson et al., 2017; Kaur et al., 2017; Kennedy et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CRY2-mCherry has been used to study the dynamics of Wnt and EGF signaling.
source: This basic unit of CRY2-mCherry attached to a variety of proteins have, for instance, been used to study cortical actin dynamics in cell contractility during tissue morphogenesis, the dynamics of Wnt and EGF signaling, plasma membrane composition and transcriptional regulation (Bugaj et al., 2018; Bugaj et al., 2015; Guglielmi et al., 2015; Huang et al., 2017; Idevall-Hagren et al., 2012; Johnson et al., 2017; Kaur et al., 2017; Kennedy et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A light-inducible system for the formation and dissolution of Aβ oligomers was generated in Drosophila melanogaster, Caenorhabditis elegans and Danio rerio.
source: Specifically, we generated an in vivo, light-dependent, oligomerization switch for the formation and dissolution of Aβ oligomers in Drosophila melanogaster, Caenorhabditis elegans and Danio rerio (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Transgenic animals expressing Aβ1–42 fused to Cryptochrome 2 and mCherry (Aβ-CRY2-mCh) were generated.
source: We generated transgenic animals expressing the 42-amino-acid human Aβ peptide (Aβ1–42) fused to Cryptochrome 2 and the fluorescent protein mCherry (Aβ-CRY2-mCh, Figure 1a, please note the relative sizes).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Drosophila lines expressing Aβ-CRY2-mCh were under the control of the GAL4/UAS system.
source: Drosophila lines were under the control of the GAL4/UAS system (Brand and Perrimon, 1993) and expressed either ubiquitously via AD-Gal4 driver (Figure 1b–c) or specifically in neurons using Elav-Gal4 driver (Figure 1d–e, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figures 1b-e.

claim: C. elegans lines expressing Aβ-CRY2-mCh were made with the heat shock promoter.
source: C. elegans lines were made with the heat shock promoter (Figure 1f–h, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figures 1f-h.

claim: Clusters of mCh fluorescence formed in Drosophila embryos exposed to 488 nm light.
source: We observed clusters of mCh fluorescence forming in embryos exposed to 488 nm light, but fewer in embryos that were not exposed to blue light (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Videos 1–2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Videos 1–2.

claim: Fewer mCh fluorescence clusters formed in Drosophila embryos that were not exposed to blue light.
source: We observed clusters of mCh fluorescence forming in embryos exposed to 488 nm light, but fewer in embryos that were not exposed to blue light (Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Videos 1–2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Videos 1–2.

claim: An increase in clusters was observed in C. elegans worms exposed to blue light over their siblings not exposed to blue light.
source: We observed an increase in clusters in worms exposed to blue light over their siblings not exposed to blue light.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Heat-shock treatment in transgenic C. elegans strain CL4176 reduced Aβ-mediated paralysis and Aβ oligomerization.
source: In particular, heat-shock treatment in another transgenic C. elegans strain, CL4176, reduced Aβ-mediated paralysis and Aβ oligomerization (Winblad, 1989; Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Overexpression of chaperone protein suppressed Aβ-toxicity in C. elegans.
source: Overexpression of chaperone protein suppressed Aβ-toxicity in C. elegans (Fonte et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Transgenic animals that had been heat-shocked had significantly higher Aβ levels compared to non-heat-shocked animals.
source: We found that transgenic animals in both heat-shock (Aβ HS L) and non-heat-shock (Aβ -HS L) condition expressed detectable Aβ-CRY2-mCh protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), however animals that had been heat-shocked had significantly higher Aβ levels compared to non-heat-shocked animals, suggesting that heat-shock, as intended, drove higher level of Aβ expression and that this was not compensated for by secondary induction of chaperones.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Heat-shock drove higher level of Aβ expression and this was not compensated for by secondary induction of chaperones.
source: We found that transgenic animals in both heat-shock (Aβ HS L) and non-heat-shock (Aβ -HS L) condition expressed detectable Aβ-CRY2-mCh protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), however animals that had been heat-shocked had significantly higher Aβ levels compared to non-heat-shocked animals, suggesting that heat-shock, as intended, drove higher level of Aβ expression and that this was not compensated for by secondary induction of chaperones.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Intracellular Aβ aggregates were observed using a direct stain for Aβ aggregates.
source: Even though the CRY2 system predominantly oligomerizes, we also observed the formation of intracellular Aβ aggregates, using a direct stain for Aβ aggregates (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Aβ aggregation was not reversible as had previously been observed for signaling molecules.
source: Importantly, we observed that Aβ aggregation was not reversible as had previously been observed for signaling molecules (Huang et al., 2017; Johnson et al., 2017; Kaur et al., 2017), rather CRY2 appeared to initiate clustering leading to Aβ bundles that did not come apart once blue light was turned off.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and comparison to previous literature.

claim: CRY2 appeared to initiate clustering leading to Aβ bundles that did not come apart once blue light was turned off.
source: Importantly, we observed that Aβ aggregation was not reversible as had previously been observed for signaling molecules (Huang et al., 2017; Johnson et al., 2017; Kaur et al., 2017), rather CRY2 appeared to initiate clustering leading to Aβ bundles that did not come apart once blue light was turned off.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Turning on blue light alone without the transgene expression did not lead to any Aβ expression or cluster formation.
source: We further confirmed that turning on blue light alone without the transgene expression did not lead to any Aβ expression or cluster formation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b, Ab HS L vs Ab –HS L), suggesting that the oligomerization process was CRY2-specific and not an artifact of light.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2b.

claim: The oligomerization process was CRY2-specific and not an artifact of light.
source: We further confirmed that turning on blue light alone without the transgene expression did not lead to any Aβ expression or cluster formation (Figure 1—figure supplement 2b, Ab HS L vs Ab –HS L), suggesting that the oligomerization process was CRY2-specific and not an artifact of light.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2b.

claim: Aβ-CRY2-mCh showed a much slower recovery of fluorescence post-bleaching compared to Arm-CRY2-mCh.
source: When compared to an unrelated CRY2 construct, we observed a very slow recovery for Aβ-CRY2-mCh compared to Arm-CRY2-mCh (Figure 2; Kaur et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The Aβ-CRY2-mCh transgene was functional in both Drosophila and C. elegans.
source: Together, our results showed that the Aβ-CRY2-mCh transgene was functional in both organisms, with a high specificity to blue light inducing irreversible oligomerization of Aβ.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Blue light induces irreversible oligomerization of Aβ with high specificity.
source: Together, our results showed that the Aβ-CRY2-mCh transgene was functional in both organisms, with a high specificity to blue light inducing irreversible oligomerization of Aβ.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Flies expressing Aβ-CRY2-mCh exposed to light died much more quickly with half the mean and maximum lifespans compared to those reared in the dark.
source: In both cases, flies exposed to light died much more quickly with half the mean and maximum lifespans (Figure 3a–b) compared to those reared in the dark.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figures 3a-b.

claim: C. elegans expressing Aβ-CRY2-mCh showed markedly decreased lifespans under light conditions compared to those kept in dark conditions.
source: Under light conditions, C. elegans showed markedly decreased lifespans as compared to the transgenic C. elegans kept in dark conditions (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The lifespan decrease in animals exposed to light was reversible, as taking animals exposed to light for 24 days and moving them into darkness showed a recovery of their lifespan.
source: Most significantly, we observed that the lifespan decrease was reversible, as taking animals exposed to light for 24 days and moving them into darkness showed a recovery of their lifespan, or a rescue (Figure 3a–b).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figures 3a-b.

claim: Fitness was severely decreased in light-exposed flies and worms as quantified by fertility and locomotive assays.
source: To ensure that these reduced lifespans were physiological, we examined the fitness of the animals. Fitness was severely decreased in light-exposed flies and worms as quantified by fertility and locomotive assays (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Light-induced Aβ oligomerization caused further impairment in sensorimotor function of transgenic Aβ nematodes.
source: Interestingly, light-induced Aβ oligomerization caused further impairment in sensorimotor function of transgenic Aβ nematodes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Light-induced oligomerization of Aβ affected lifespan, fitness, and impaired complex sensorimotor function and behavior.
source: These results suggesed that light-induced oligomerization of Aβ not only affected lifespan and fitness, but also impaired complex sensorimotor function and behavior.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Embryos expressing Aβ in only the nervous system developed at a normal pace and did not show any morphogenetic defects in the absence of blue light.
source: Embryos expressing Aβ in only the nervous system developed at a normal pace and did not show any morphogenetic defects and even hatched in the absence of blue light (Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Video 1.

claim: Sibling embryos exposed to blue laser light arrested in late neurogenesis stages where the central nervous system stopped developing and the embryos died.
source: In contrast, sibling embryos exposed to blue laser light arrested in late neurogenesis stages where the central nervous system stopped developing and the embryos died (Video 2 and Figure 4, Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Video 2 and Figures 4, 1—figure supplement 3, and 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Embryos exposed to blue light showed a variety of abnormalities in the positioning of neurons and glial cells.
source: These embryos showed a variety of abnormalities in the positioning of neurons and glial cells (Compare to complete normal development, Video 3) suggesting that light-induced Aβ oligomerization caused physical, structural damage that affects neuronal development.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Video 3.

claim: Light-induced Aβ oligomerization caused physical, structural damage that affects neuronal development.
source: These embryos showed a variety of abnormalities in the positioning of neurons and glial cells (Compare to complete normal development, Video 3) suggesting that light-induced Aβ oligomerization caused physical, structural damage that affects neuronal development.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Video 3.

claim: Expression of Aβ alone, without light-induced Aβ oligomerization, led to a small increase in inflammatory markers.
source: Expression of Aβ alone, without light-induced Aβ oligomerization, led to a small increase in inflammatory markers (Figure 4e; Westfall et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 4e.

claim: In embryos exposed to light, two inflammatory markers increased to a much greater level.
source: In embryos exposed to light, two of these markers increased to a much greater level (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 4e.

claim: A significant reduction in the number of mitochondria was observed in light-treated Aβ animals.
source: We observed a significant reduction in the number of mitochondria in light-treated Aβ animals (Figure 4f).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 4f.

claim: Markers of oxidative damage in light and dark exposed C. elegans showed differential expression of antioxidant defense genes, specifically Catalase, Trx-2 and Sod-3.
source: Markers of oxidative damage in light and dark exposed C. elegans showed differential expression of antioxidant defense genes, specifically Catalase, Trx-2 and Sod-3, suggestive of the occurrence of oxidative stress induced by Aβ oligomerization (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Oxidative stress is induced by Aβ oligomerization.
source: Markers of oxidative damage in light and dark exposed C. elegans showed differential expression of antioxidant defense genes, specifically Catalase, Trx-2 and Sod-3, suggestive of the occurrence of oxidative stress induced by Aβ oligomerization (Figure 5).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Light-induced Aβ oligomerization phenocopied many of the hallmarks of AD.
source: These results suggested that light-induced Aβ oligomerization phenocopied many of the hallmarks of AD.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Heat-shocked mutants exposed to light (Aβ HS L) had lower ATP levels compared to the non-transgenic control (Ctrl -HS D).
source: Heat-shocked mutants exposed to light (Aβ HS L) had lower ATP levels compared to the non-transgenic control (Ctrl -HS D) (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 6.

claim: Heat-shocked mutants in the dark condition (Aβ HS D) did not show any significant differences in ATP level compared to the non-transgenic control.
source: However, heat-shocked mutants in the dark condition (Aβ HS D) did not show any significant differences in ATP level compared to the non-transgenic control.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Presence of Aβ alone is insufficient to induce ATP deficits.
source: This result suggested that presence of Aβ alone is insufficient to induce ATP deficits, and that light-induced oligomerization of Aβ is required for the defect to manifest.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data presented.

claim: Light-induced oligomerization of Aβ is required for ATP deficits to manifest.
source: This result suggested that presence of Aβ alone is insufficient to induce ATP deficits, and that light-induced oligomerization of Aβ is required for the defect to manifest.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data presented.

claim: Aβ expression alone was insufficient to affect the nematodes' maximum respiratory capacity.
source: Aβ expression alone was also insufficient to affect the nematodes' maximum respiratory capacity, as heat-shocked mutants in the dark condition (Aβ HS D) did not display differences in maximum and spare respiration capacity compared to control animals (Ctrl -HS D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Light-induced Aβ oligomerization significantly reduced maximum respiration capacity in C. elegans.
source: However, light-induced Aβ oligomerization significantly reduced maximum respiration capacity in C. elegans.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Heat-shocked mutants in the light condition (Aβ HS L) displayed significantly lower maximum and spare respiration capacity compared to controls (Ctrl -HS D) and to heat-shocked mutants in the dark condition (Aβ HS D).
source: Heat-shocked mutants in the light condition (Aβ HS L) displayed significantly lower maximum and spare respiration capacity compared to controls (Ctrl -HS D) and to heat-shocked mutants in the dark condition (Aβ HS D) (Figure 6b–d).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figures 6b-d.

claim: Metabolic deficits were mediated by light-induced Aβ oligomerization.
source: Together, these results highlighted the metabolic differences between the two conditions and showed that metabolic deficits were mediated by light-induced Aβ oligomerization.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Heat-shock treatment does not affect ATP levels in control animals.
source: We found that heat-shock treatment does not affect ATP levels in the control animals, suggesting that the ATP detriment was a result of Aβ expression, but not heat-shock treatment (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The ATP detriment was a result of Aβ expression, but not heat-shock treatment.
source: We found that heat-shock treatment does not affect ATP levels in the control animals, suggesting that the ATP detriment was a result of Aβ expression, but not heat-shock treatment (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Heat-shock treatment appears to reduce the respiratory capacity of control animals.
source: On the other hand, heat-shock treatment appears to reduce the respiratory capacity of the control animals, suggesting that the decline in respiratory capacity was mediated by both heat-shock and Aβ expression (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 6c.

claim: The decline in respiratory capacity was mediated by both heat-shock and Aβ expression.
source: On the other hand, heat-shock treatment appears to reduce the respiratory capacity of the control animals, suggesting that the decline in respiratory capacity was mediated by both heat-shock and Aβ expression (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Light treatment, which induces oligomerization, worsened the phenotypic and metabolic detriments in the transgenic animals.
source: Comparing the heat-shocked transgenic animals in light and dark conditions, we found that light treatment, which induces oligomerization, worsened the phenotypic and metabolic detriments in the transgenic animals.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Regardless of the effects of heat-shock and chaperone induction, oligomerization still negatively impacted the phenotypes.
source: This suggested that regardless of the effects of heat-shock and chaperone induction, oligomerization still negatively impacted the phenotypes.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data presented.

claim: Li+ is used for treatment of neurological conditions.
source: The drug Li+ is used for treatment of neurological conditions (Licht, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: A high drinking water Li+ concentration correlated with lower human mortality.
source: A high drinking water Li+ concentration correlated with lower human mortality (Zarse et al., 2011), and Li+ increased the lifespan of C. elegans and Drosophila (Castillo-Quan et al., 2016; McColl et al., 2008; Tam et al., 2014; Teo et al., 2020a; Teo et al., 2020b; Zarse et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Li+ increased the lifespan of C. elegans and Drosophila.
source: A high drinking water Li+ concentration correlated with lower human mortality (Zarse et al., 2011), and Li+ increased the lifespan of C. elegans and Drosophila (Castillo-Quan et al., 2016; McColl et al., 2008; Tam et al., 2014; Teo et al., 2020a; Teo et al., 2020b; Zarse et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The molecular mechanisms by which Li+ functions include inhibition of inositol monophosphotase (IMPA) and glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK-3).
source: The molecular mechanisms by which Li+ functions include inhibition of inositol monophosphotase (IMPA) and glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK-3) (Kerr et al., 2018), reduction of oxidative damage (Kasuya et al., 2009; Kerr et al., 2017; Khan et al., 2015) and longevity via a GSK-3/NRF-2 dependent, hormetic mechanism (Castillo-Quan et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Li+ reduces oxidative damage.
source: The molecular mechanisms by which Li+ functions include inhibition of inositol monophosphotase (IMPA) and glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK-3) (Kerr et al., 2018), reduction of oxidative damage (Kasuya et al., 2009; Kerr et al., 2017; Khan et al., 2015) and longevity via a GSK-3/NRF-2 dependent, hormetic mechanism (Castillo-Quan et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Li+ promotes longevity via a GSK-3/NRF-2 dependent, hormetic mechanism.
source: The molecular mechanisms by which Li+ functions include inhibition of inositol monophosphotase (IMPA) and glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK-3) (Kerr et al., 2018), reduction of oxidative damage (Kasuya et al., 2009; Kerr et al., 2017; Khan et al., 2015) and longevity via a GSK-3/NRF-2 dependent, hormetic mechanism (Castillo-Quan et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The Wnt signaling pathway plays a role in modulating AD pathology and its progression.
source: Among the mechanisms for neuroprotection, the Wnt signaling pathway plays a role in modulating AD pathology and its progression (De Ferrari et al., 2003; Jin et al., 2017; Parr et al., 2015; Toledo and Inestrosa, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Activation of Wnt signaling through lithium (Li+) treatment attenuated Aβ aggregation and increased the lifespan of Aβ models.
source: Activation of Wnt signaling through lithium (Li+) treatment attenuated Aβ aggregation and increased the lifespan of Aβ models (Toledo and Inestrosa, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: By inhibiting the enzyme glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK-3), Li+ compounds drive the downstream production of intracellular β-catenin activating the Wnt–β-catenin signaling pathway.
source: By inhibiting the enzyme glycogen synthase kinase-3 (GSK-3), Li+ compounds drive the downstream production of intracellular β-catenin activating the Wnt–β-catenin signaling pathway (Klein and Melton, 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Li+ treatment through Wnt activation rescued behavioral impairment and neurodegeneration induced by Aβ fibrils.
source: Li+ treatment through Wnt activation also rescued behavioral impairment and neurodegeneration induced by Aβ fibrils (De Ferrari et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Drosophila exposed to light, but consuming Li+ had significantly increased lifespans.
source: Drosophila exposed to light, but consuming Li+ had significantly increased lifespans, suggesting both a rescue effect induced by Li+ (Figure 3a–b), and that the optogenetic model can be used for inducible expression drug testing.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figures 3a-b.

claim: The optogenetic model can be used for inducible expression drug testing.
source: Drosophila exposed to light, but consuming Li+ had significantly increased lifespans, suggesting both a rescue effect induced by Li+ (Figure 3a–b), and that the optogenetic model can be used for inducible expression drug testing.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data shown in Figures 3a-b.

claim: Aβ clusters formed upon stimulation with blue light in HEK293 cells transfected with Aβ-CRY2-mCh.
source: We extended this assay to HEK293 cells transfected with Aβ-CRY2-mCh where Aβ clusters formed upon stimulation with blue light (Figure 7a).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 7a.

claim: The number of clusters per cell was greatly reduced by the addition of Li+ or the specific GSK3 inhibitor CHIR99021.
source: The number of clusters per cell was greatly reduced by the addition of Li+ or the specific GSK3 inhibitor CHIR99021, but CHIR99021 additionally reduced the signal intensity of the clusters (Figure 7b–c, quantified 7d).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figures 7b-d.

claim: CHIR99021 additionally reduced the signal intensity of the clusters.
source: The number of clusters per cell was greatly reduced by the addition of Li+ or the specific GSK3 inhibitor CHIR99021, but CHIR99021 additionally reduced the signal intensity of the clusters (Figure 7b–c, quantified 7d).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figures 7b-d.

claim: A zebrafish permanent line with UAS:Aβ-CRY2-mCh was generated in the transgenic TgBAC(gng8:GAL4)c416 background.
source: We generated a zebrafish permanent line with UAS:Aβ-CRY2-mCh in the transgenic TgBAC(gng8:GAL4)c416 background (Hong et al., 2013) that limited expression to a few cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: A diffuse mCh fluorescence was observed in a small subset of neurons in the olfactory epithelium, the interpeduncular nucleus and in a few neurons sparsely distributed in the forebrain at 5 dpf.
source: We observed a diffuse mCh fluorescence in a small subset of neurons in the olfactory epithelium, the interpeduncular nucleus and in a few neurons sparsely distributed in the forebrain at 5 dpf.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Upon blue light exposure (488 nM) the detectable intensity of the fluorescence increased rapidly.
source: Upon blue light exposure (488 nM) the detectable intensity of the fluorescence increased rapidly (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Several neurons among those expressing appeared to bleb and began to die within 40 to 50 min of initial exposure to the blue light.
source: Several neurons among those expressing appeared to bleb and began to die within 40 to 50 min of initial exposure to the blue light (Video 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Video 4.

claim: Such damage was not observable in matched controls expressing Aβ-mCh driven by a CMV promotor lacking the CRY2 protein.
source: Such damage was not observable in matched controls expressing Aβ-mCh driven by a CMV promotor lacking the CRY2 protein (Video 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Video 5.

claim: Aβ-CRY2-mCh expressing zebrafish embryos showed lower maximum and spare respiration capacity compared to un-injected control.
source: Similar to the impairments observed in C. elegans, Aβ-CRY2-mCh expressing embryos showed lower maximum and spare respiration capacity compared to un-injected control (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 8.

claim: Light exposure of Aβ-CRY2-mCh expressing zebrafish embryos caused a significant reduction in ATP levels.
source: In addition, light exposure of Aβ-CRY2-mCh expressing embryos caused a significant reduction in ATP levels (Figure 8a).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 8a.

claim: Aggregation of Aβ has been studied extensively.
source: Aggregation of Aβ has been studied extensively, but our results represent the first study to demonstrate that induced oligomerization of intracellular Aβ can be used to separate different pathologies (induced by Aβ oligomerization vs expression alone).
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of the field.

claim: This study represents the first to demonstrate that induced oligomerization of intracellular Aβ can be used to separate different pathologies (induced by Aβ oligomerization vs expression alone).
source: Aggregation of Aβ has been studied extensively, but our results represent the first study to demonstrate that induced oligomerization of intracellular Aβ can be used to separate different pathologies (induced by Aβ oligomerization vs expression alone).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the primary finding of the study.

claim: A second approach to making inducible aggregates using a chemically controlled fluorescent protein has been published, but not yet widely tested.
source: A second approach to making inducible aggregates using a chemically controlled fluorescent protein has been published, but not yet widely tested (Miyazaki et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Other previous approaches lacked an inducible oligomerization tool and could only demonstrate Aβ oligomers' toxicity through exogenous injection of Aβ oligomers.
source: Other previous approaches lacked an inducible oligomerization tool and could only demonstrate Aβ oligomers' toxicity through exogenous injection of Aβ oligomers (Mroczko et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: CRY2 initiated clustering of Aβ appeared to be irreversible likely due to the structure of the aggregates.
source: Despite the reversibility of CRY2 clustering in previous findings, we find that CRY2 initiated clustering of Aβ appeared to be irreversible likely due to the structure of the aggregates (Antzutkin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and comparison to previous literature.

claim: Aβ oligomers induce oxidative stress and inflammation.
source: Consistent with existing literature showing that Aβ oligomers induce oxidative stress and inflammation (Butterfield et al., 2013; Forloni and Balducci, 2018), we show that light-induced oligomerization of Aβ, but not Aβ expression alone, is necessary for the metabolic defects, loss of mitochondria and inflammation in C. elegans and Drosophila.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Light-induced oligomerization of Aβ, but not Aβ expression alone, is necessary for the metabolic defects, loss of mitochondria and inflammation in C. elegans and Drosophila.
source: Consistent with existing literature showing that Aβ oligomers induce oxidative stress and inflammation (Butterfield et al., 2013; Forloni and Balducci, 2018), we show that light-induced oligomerization of Aβ, but not Aβ expression alone, is necessary for the metabolic defects, loss of mitochondria and inflammation in C. elegans and Drosophila.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Light-induced oligomerization leads to physical damage of the nervous system in D. rerio, resembling the loss of brain tissue in AD.
source: Light-induced oligomerization also leads to physical damage of the nervous system in D. rerio, resembling the loss of brain tissue in AD (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The embryonic assay for physical damage phenocopies brain lesions only to some degree as the extent of the damage is enhanced by the forces applied to the developing neural tissue.
source: The embryonic assay for physical damage phenocopies brain lesions only to some degree as the extent of the damage is enhanced by the forces applied to the developing neural tissue.
evidence: This is a discussion of the limitations of the model.

claim: The irreversibility of Aβ aggregates once initiated hints at intrinsic properties that may be unique or unusual to this peptide.
source: The irreversibility of Aβ aggregates once initiated as seen here, also hints at intrinsic properties that may be unique or unusual to this peptide and warrants further investigation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the experimental observations.

claim: The optogenetic Aβ model is likely to prove a good model for testing anti-aggregation compounds.
source: It is also likely to prove a good model for testing anti-aggregation compounds.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of the model.

claim: The optogenetic strategy will serve as an attractive tool for carrying out drug screens and mechanistic studies for the treatment of AD.
source: We anticipate that our approach will serve as an attractive tool for carrying out drug screens and mechanistic studies for the treatment of AD.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of the model.

claim: The optogenetic strategy could be optimally positioned to gain insights into the unresolved mechanism of Aβ - whether oligomerization and subsequent accumulation or lack of effective clearance underpins AD pathologies.
source: This optogenetic strategy will also undoubtedly complement other techniques due to the high level of spatiotemporal specificity. For example, it could be optimally positioned to gain insights into the unresolved mechanism of Aβ - whether oligomerization and subsequent accumulation or lack of effective clearance underpins AD pathologies.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of the model.

claim: The separation of two phases of AD progression suggests that single drug treatments will not suffice, and perhaps combinatorial approaches should be tried.
source: The separation of two phases of AD progression also suggests that single drug treatments will not suffice, and perhaps combinatorial approaches should be tried.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the experimental findings.
